headline: Navana Group Vice Chairman Sajedul Islam arrested from Banani residence
summary: Police arrested the business leader during a raid at his Dhaka home following an outstanding arrest warrant.
details: Police arrested Navana Group Vice Chairman Sajedul Islam Shuvro from his residence in Dhaka's Banani area on Tuesday morning.
The operation took place at a house in Block D around 7:00 am, according to Mahbubur Rahman, officer-in-charge of Tejgaon Industrial Area Police Station.
The arrest was made based on an existing warrant, and Sajedul was sent to court shortly after the operation.
Police alleged that they faced obstruction while entering the building and that security personnel did not cooperate during the raid, which began around 11:00 pm the previous night.
The specific details of the case under which the warrant was issued have not yet been confirmed.
caption:
Navana Group Vice Chairman Sajedul Islam Shuvro has been arrested from his Banani residence.

Police arrested Navana Group Vice Chairman Sajedul Islam Shuvro from his residence in Dhaka's Banani area on Tuesday morning.

The operation took place at a house in Block D around 7:00 am, according to Mahbubur Rahman, officer-in-charge of Tejgaon Industrial Area Police Station.

The arrest was made based on an existing warrant, and Sajedul was sent to court shortly after the operation.

Police alleged that they faced obstruction while entering the building and that security personnel did not cooperate during the raid, which began around 11:00 pm the previous night.

The specific details of the case under which the warrant was issued have not yet been confirmed.

headline: Dhaka ranks 9th among world’s most polluted cities
summary: The capital city continues to struggle with severe air quality issues, placing it among the top ten most polluted cities globally.
details: Dhaka has been ranked as the 9th most polluted city in the world. This ranking highlights the critical state of air quality in the capital, posing significant health risks to millions of residents.
The pollution levels in Dhaka often exceed safe limits recommended by international health organizations, contributing to respiratory illnesses and other long-term health complications.
While other cities like Lahore also face extreme pollution, Dhaka's consistent presence in the top ten underscores a systemic environmental crisis.
Efforts to curb emissions from vehicles, construction dust, and industrial waste remain a primary challenge for city authorities to improve the air quality.
caption:
Dhaka is now the 9th most polluted city on Earth. The air we breathe is reaching critical levels.
